You could use the
Label
and
Jump To Label
commands:
Label
lets you define a "name" to jump to. Without Jump to Label, it does nothing.
Jump to Label
goes immediately to the named Label (if it exists in the current event).
These commands can be helpful for designing non-linear events.
As a general rule, Don't Repeat Yourself, i.e. try to avoid copy+pasting the same thing to many places. For a diary that displays pictures based on certain variables/switches:
Maybe the optional parts can be split into their own picture. E.g.
Variable 1 > 5: "I've found the magic bell. I should bring it back to Harold."
Switch 1 is ON: "I rang the bell and found myself in a strange world. I need to escape!"
I.e. 2 different pictures on screen at the same time. It sounds like maybe you already do this?
If some combinations show the same picture then you can give each possible result a unique value, or "index". You can use another variable to determine the quest's current index, e.g.
Variable 2 = 0
If Variable 1 > 5
Variable 2 += 1
If Switch 1 is ON
Variable 2 += 2
Etc.
Then just show the picture based on Variable 2.
If you have a different image for every different combination of variable/switch, then you need to branch that many times. In that case there is no workaround.

The
Show Picture
command shows a picture with an ID (1~100). So you can show up to 100 pictures at the same time. To show more than 1 picture, use more than 1 Show Picture command. If 2 pictures overlap, the one with higher ID shows on top.
Example:
Spoiler
Comment: Set up diary pictures.
Show Picture 7: Diary_Background
Erase Picture: 8
Erase Picture: 9
Comment: Stage 1 content.
If Variable 1 = 1
Show Picture 8: Diary1
If Switch 1 is ON
Show Picture 9: Diary1_S1
Jump to Label: Done
Comment: Stage 2 content.
If Variable 1 = 2
Show Picture 8: Diary2
If Switch 2 is ON
Show Picture 9: Diary2_S2
Jump to Label: Done
Label: Done
Comment: Wait for player input, then clear.
Show Text: Text = (Nothing), Background = Transparent.
Erase Picture: 7
Erase Picture: 8
Erase Picture: 9
Here, I've used picture ID 7 for the background, 8 for the main content, and 9 for optional content.
